takes.prompt: Genre: warm orchestral video game soundtrack in the spirit of Studio Ghibli and Ori and the Blind Forest. BPM: 88. Key: D major. Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. Setting: Pine Hollow, a misty pine forest at dawn - wonder first, quiet adventure second, a little melancholy underneath. Arrangement: a lyrical flute and oboe melody over legato strings and harp arpeggios; pizzicato basses and cellos walk underneath, and a soft steady pulse of frame drum, low toms and light timpani runs under the whole piece from the second bar to the end. No fade-out: the last bar is as full as the rest. Production: warm concert-hall reverb.

Genre: warm orchestral video game soundtrack in the spirit of Studio Ghibli and Ori and the Blind Forest. BPM: 100. Key: D major. Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. Setting: Driftwood Isle, a sunlit island of pale sand and turquoise water - wonder first, breezy seafaring adventure second, a little melancholy underneath. Arrangement: a buoyant clarinet and violin melody over rippling harp, celesta and bright strings; plucked double basses and a steady light groove of tambourine, frame drum and soft snare run under the whole piece from the second bar to the end. No fade-out: the last bar is as full as the rest. Production: bright, wide hall reverb.

Genre: video game main title theme, warm cinematic orchestra in the spirit of Joe Hisaishi and Ori and the Blind Forest. BPM: 92. Key: D major. Instrumental only, no vocals, no lead choir. The main theme of Wildshard, a world that arrives one chunk at a time - wonder first, adventure second, a little melancholy underneath. Arrangement: a memorable, hummable melody introduced by solo flute over harp, then taken up by full strings and French horns with timpani and a steady percussion pulse; it swells to a soaring climax and ends on a resolved final chord. Production: rich concert-hall reverb.
